subproblem.title: Interchanging time and space derivatives of a family that is C² at a point (Schwarz)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, t ∈ ℝ and y ∈ ℝᴺ, and suppose (s,x) ↦ Φ s x is C² at (t,y) (ContDiffAt ℝ 2). Then the map s ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y, from ℝ to the continuous linear maps ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, has derivative fderiv ℝ (x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t) y at s = t.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (Φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N) (t : ℝ) (y : Rn N), ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun p : ℝ × Rn N ↦ Φ p.1 p.2) (t, y) → HasDerivAt (fun s ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y) (fderiv ℝ (fun x ↦ deriv (fun s ↦ Φ s x) t) y) t
subproblem.natural_proof:
Provenance: the mixed-partials step of the parent proof of variation_deformation_calculus: ∂_t Dφ_t = D(∂_tφ), by symmetry of the second derivative. The parent uses it at (0,y), at every (t,y) with |t| < 1, and for the family ∂_tφ. Here it is stated once, for a general family Φ at an arbitrary point (t,y), under the pointwise hypothesis that F is C² at (t,y). The proof below is self-contained.

Notation. F(s,x) := Φ s x. DF(p) := fderiv ℝ F p. D²F(p) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) p, a continuous linear map from ℝ × ℝᴺ to the continuous linear maps ℝ × ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ. e₀ := (1,0). inr v := (0,v).

1. Partial derivatives at points of differentiability. Let F be differentiable at (s,x).
 (a) The map x′ ↦ (s,x′) has derivative inr, and Φ s = F ∘ (x′ ↦ (s,x′)). By the chain rule, fderiv ℝ (Φ s) x = DF(s,x) ∘ inr.
 (b) The map s′ ↦ (s′,x) has derivative e₀ at s, and s′ ↦ Φ s′ x equals s′ ↦ F(s′,x). By the chain rule, deriv (s′ ↦ Φ s′ x) s = DF(s,x) e₀.
2. F is C² near (t,y). F is C² at (t,y) and the exponent 2 is finite, so F is C² at every point of some neighbourhood W of (t,y) (Mathlib ContDiffAt.eventually). In particular F is differentiable at every point of W.
3. DF is differentiable at (t,y). F is C² at (t,y), so DF is C¹ at (t,y) (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right, using 1 + 1 ≤ 2). Hence DF is differentiable at (t,y) with derivative D²F(t,y).
4. Localisation. The maps s ↦ (s,y) and x ↦ (t,x) are continuous and take the value (t,y) at s = t and at x = y. So (s,y) ∈ W for all s near t, and (t,x) ∈ W for all x near y.
 - By 1(a) and 2, fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y = DF(s,y) ∘ inr for all s near t.
 - By 1(b) and 2, deriv (s′ ↦ Φ s′ x) t = DF(t,x) e₀ for all x near y.
5. Derivative in s. By 3 and the chain rule along s ↦ (s,y), whose derivative is e₀, the map s ↦ DF(s,y) has derivative D²F(t,y) e₀ at t (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt). Compose on the right with the constant map s ↦ inr, using the product rule for composition of continuous linear maps (HasDerivAt.clm_comp). The constant factor contributes DF(t,y) ∘ 0 = 0. So s ↦ DF(s,y) ∘ inr has derivative (D²F(t,y) e₀) ∘ inr at t.
6. Derivative in x. By 3 and the chain rule along x ↦ (t,x), whose derivative is inr, the map x ↦ DF(t,x) has derivative D²F(t,y) ∘ inr at y. Now apply the continuous linear evaluation B ↦ B e₀. So x ↦ DF(t,x) e₀ has derivative v ↦ D²F(t,y)(inr v)(e₀) at y.
7. By 4, x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t coincides near y with x ↦ DF(t,x) e₀. By 6, and because derivatives depend only on germs (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), fderiv ℝ (x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t) y is the linear map v ↦ D²F(t,y)(inr v)(e₀).
8. Symmetry (Schwarz).
 - F is C² at (t,y), and over ℝ the smoothness threshold minSmoothness ℝ 2 equals 2. So D²F(t,y) is symmetric: D²F(t,y)(a)(b) = D²F(t,y)(b)(a) for all a, b ∈ ℝ × ℝᴺ.
 - This is Mathlib ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, in Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Symmetric.lean. The frozen header does not import that file, so the Lean proof must add the import.
 - Take a = inr v and b = e₀ and use step 7: fderiv ℝ (x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t) y v = D²F(t,y)(e₀)(inr v) for every v. That is, fderiv ℝ (x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t) y = (D²F(t,y) e₀) ∘ inr.
9. Conclusion. By 4, s ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y coincides near t with s ↦ DF(s,y) ∘ inr. By 5, the latter has derivative (D²F(t,y) e₀) ∘ inr at t. So, by HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq, s ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y has derivative (D²F(t,y) e₀) ∘ inr at t. By 8 this derivative equals fderiv ℝ (x ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t) y.
proof_key_steps: F(s,x) = Φ s x is C², hence differentiable, on a neighbourhood of (t,y) (ContDiffAt.eventually). DF is differentiable at (t,y) with derivative D²F(t,y).
Near t, fderiv ℝ (Φ s) y = DF(s,y) ∘ inr, and this has s-derivative D²F(t,y)(e₀) ∘ inr at t.
Near y, deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t = DF(t,x)e₀, and this has x-derivative v ↦ D²F(t,y)(inr v)(e₀) at y.
Symmetry of D²F(t,y) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt) identifies the two derivatives. Conclude with HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly states interchange at arbitrary (t,y). Finite-order ContDiffAt supplies the neighborhood needed for both germ identities. Differentiating DF along the two embeddings and applying symmetry identifies the continuous-linear-map derivatives; eventual equality transfers the result. Every step is supplied, non-circular and sufficient for formalization.

subproblem.title: Spatial and time partial derivatives of a family that is jointly C^n on an open set are C^m there (m + 1 ≤ n)
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, let O ⊆ ℝ × ℝᴺ be open, and let m, n ∈ WithTop ℕ∞ (smoothness exponents) satisfy m + 1 ≤ n. Suppose (t,x) ↦ Φ t x is C^n on O (ContDiffOn ℝ n). Then the spatial derivative (t,x) ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ t) x and the time derivative (t,x) ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t are both C^m on O.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (Φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N) (O : Set (ℝ × Rn N)) (m n : WithTop ℕ∞), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ n (fun p : ℝ × Rn N ↦ Φ p.1 p.2) O → m + 1 ≤ n → ContDiffOn ℝ m (fun p : ℝ × Rn N ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ p.1) p.2) O ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ m (fun p : ℝ × Rn N ↦ deriv (fun s ↦ Φ s p.2) p.1) O
subproblem.natural_proof:
Provenance: the joint-regularity step of the parent proof of variation_deformation_calculus, which shows A(t,x) = Dφ_t(x) is C^{r−1} on (−1,1) × U. It also covers the regularity of the time derivative ∂_tφ that the parent uses for C³ families. Here it is stated for a general family Φ, a general open set O and exponents with m + 1 ≤ n. The proof below is self-contained.

Notation. F : ℝ × ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, F(t,x) := Φ t x. DF(p) := fderiv ℝ F p, a continuous linear map ℝ × ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ. e₀ := (1,0) ∈ ℝ × ℝᴺ. inr : ℝᴺ → ℝ × ℝᴺ, inr v := (0,v), a continuous linear map.

1. Differentiability on O. In WithTop ℕ∞ we have 0 < 1 ≤ m + 1 ≤ n, so n ≠ 0. Let p ∈ O. Since O is open it is a neighbourhood of p, so F, which is C^n on O, is C^n at p (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). As n ≠ 0, F is differentiable at p (ContDiffAt.differentiableAt).
2. Regularity of DF. Since O is open and m + 1 ≤ n, the map p ↦ DF(p) is C^m on O (Mathlib ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen).
3. Spatial partial derivative. Let p = (t,x) ∈ O. The affine map ι_t(x′) := (t,x′) has derivative inr at x (hasFDerivAt_prodMk_right), and Φ t = F ∘ ι_t. F is differentiable at ι_t(x) = (t,x) by 1, so by the chain rule Φ t has derivative DF(t,x) ∘ inr at x. Hence fderiv ℝ (Φ t) x = DF(t,x) ∘ inr.
4. The map p ↦ DF(p) ∘ inr is C^m on O. It composes the C^m map p ↦ DF(p) of step 2 with the constant map p ↦ inr, and composing continuous-linear-map-valued C^m maps gives a C^m map (ContDiffOn.clm_comp with contDiffOn_const). By 3 it agrees at every point of O with p ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ p.1) p.2. A function that agrees on O with a function that is C^m on O is itself C^m on O (ContDiffOn.congr). Hence (t,x) ↦ fderiv ℝ (Φ t) x is C^m on O.
5. Time partial derivative. Let p = (t,x) ∈ O. The curve c_x(s) := (s,x) has derivative e₀ at t (HasDerivAt.prodMk of hasDerivAt_id and hasDerivAt_const), and s ↦ Φ s x equals F ∘ c_x. F is differentiable at c_x(t) = (t,x) by 1, so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) s ↦ Φ s x has derivative DF(t,x) e₀ at t. Hence deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t = DF(t,x) e₀.
6. The map p ↦ DF(p) e₀ is C^m on O. It applies the C^m map p ↦ DF(p) of step 2 to the constant vector e₀ (ContDiffOn.clm_apply with contDiffOn_const). By 5 it agrees at every point of O with p ↦ deriv (s ↦ Φ s p.2) p.1, so the latter is C^m on O (ContDiffOn.congr).
7. Steps 4 and 6 are the two conclusions.
proof_key_steps: F(t,x) = Φ t x is differentiable at every point of the open set O, since n ≥ 1. Also p ↦ DF(p) is C^m on O (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, using m + 1 ≤ n).
Chain rule along x′ ↦ (t,x′): fderiv ℝ (Φ t) x = DF(t,x) ∘ inr on O. Since p ↦ DF(p) ∘ inr is C^m on O, the spatial derivative is C^m on O (ContDiffOn.congr).
Chain rule along s ↦ (s,x): deriv (s ↦ Φ s x) t = DF(t,x)(1,0) on O. Since p ↦ DF(p)(1,0) is C^m on O, the time derivative is C^m on O (ContDiffOn.congr).

audit.reason: The exact type includes openness, joint C^n regularity and m + 1 ≤ n. The argument works for every stated WithTop ℕ∞ exponent: n is nonzero, DF is C^m, and chain rules identify both partial derivatives on O. Continuous-linear-map composition, evaluation and congruence prove both conclusions without another child.

subproblem.title: Initial velocity, acceleration and their spatial derivatives vanish off a closed set fixed by the family
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ (ℝᴺ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)), let K ⊆ ℝᴺ be closed, and let φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ satisfy φ t x = x for every t ∈ (−1,1) and every x ∉ K. Put X := initialVelocity φ, X(x) = deriv (s ↦ φ s x) 0, and Z := initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = deriv (t ↦ deriv (s ↦ φ s x) t) 0. Then for every x ∉ K: X(x) = 0, Z(x) = 0, fderiv ℝ X x = 0 and fderiv ℝ Z x = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (K : Set (Rn N)) (φ : ℝ → Rn N → Rn N), IsClosed K → (∀ t ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x, x ∉ K → φ t x = x) → ∀ x, x ∉ K → initialVelocity φ x = 0 ∧ initialAcceleration φ x = 0 ∧ fderiv ℝ (initialVelocity φ) x = 0 ∧ fderiv ℝ (initialAcceleration φ) x = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Provenance: part (V) of the parent proof of variation_deformation_calculus. The hypotheses are reduced to what that argument uses: K is closed (in the parent K is compact, hence closed), and φ_t = id off K for |t| < 1. The proof below is self-contained.

Notation. For x ∈ ℝᴺ put g_x(s) := φ s x and h_x(t) := deriv g_x t. By definition X(x) = initialVelocity φ x = deriv g_x 0 and Z(x) = initialAcceleration φ x = deriv h_x 0. Here deriv and fderiv are Mathlib's derivatives, which depend only on the germ of the function at the point (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq, Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).

1. Fix x ∉ K. For every s ∈ (−1,1) the hypothesis gives g_x(s) = φ s x = x.

3. Since 0 ∈ (−1,1), step 2 with t = 0 gives X(x) = deriv g_x 0 = 0.

5. Steps 1–4 apply at every point of ℝᴺ ∖ K, so X(x′) = 0 and Z(x′) = 0 for all x′ ∉ K. K is closed, so ℝᴺ ∖ K is open. For x ∉ K it is therefore a neighbourhood of x on which X and Z are identically 0. So X and Z coincide near x with the constant map 0, and fderiv ℝ X x = fderiv ℝ (fun _ ↦ 0) x = 0 and fderiv ℝ Z x = 0 (fderiv_const_apply).
